title: Focus Battery KPI Lab
content:
Purpose: short running experiment to treat attention and context-switching like a finite battery. Goal is to increase weekly deep-work hours and reduce task-switching overhead so product work (perf reductions, PR throughput) and personal wellbeing both improve.

Quick thesis: small changes to calendar hygiene + explicit RPC (Rest for Context) micro-buffers between meetings will recover 25–40% of my attention bandwidth. If deep sessions increase by 3–4 hours/week, I can land 2 medium-impact perf PRs in a sprint and reduce small-block latency work backlog.

OKR draft (personal - 6 weeks):
- Objective: Recover and spend attention intentionally to ship more high-leverage work.
  - KR1: Increase weekly focused blocks (>=60 min, no notifications) from baseline 4h -> target 9h.
  - KR2: Reduce daily context switches (phone/apps/email/code) from median 18 -> <=10.
  - KR3: Merge time-to-merge for my PRs from median 72h -> <=36h (negotiated with reviewers).
  - KR4: Ship two perf-focused PRs that measurably cut P50 token latency by >=8% on our dev harness.

Baseline measurements (week of 2025-02-10):
- Deep-focus blocks: 4.1 hours/week (tracked via RescueTime, manual notes).
- Context switches/day: median 18 (estimated from 24h activity log, noisy).
- PR time-to-merge (last 8 PRs): median 72h, mean 84h.
- Energy subjective score (1–10) at EOD: average 5.6.

Hypotheses & experiments (a/b parallel):
1) Calendar armor + 25-min buffer (RPC) before/after meetings -> fewer interrupted deep sessions. Measurement: increase in 60+ min blocks, ± change in subjective energy.
2) Inbox pause (email/slack mute) during 2 afternoon blocks -> fewer micro-switches and faster PR focus. Measurement: context switches/day and PR progress recorded in checklist.
3) Short async standup (typed, <10 min) instead of 9am meeting -> recover morning attention. Measurement: reclaimed morning 60-min block; team OK with async? (Asha to pilot).
4) Single-tasking coding sprint with explicit acceptance criteria and 30-min pairing once/week for review -> reduces rework. Measurement: time-to-merge and reviewer comment cycles.

Mini acceptance criteria for success: if after 6 weeks deep-focus blocks >=8h/w and PR time-to-merge <=36h and subjective energy >=7, mark experiment as successful and bake calendar defaults.

Weekly check-in template (use every Friday):
- Week (dates):
- Deep-hours logged (>=60m blocks):
- Median context switches/day this week:
- PRs opened/merged this week (time-to-merge):
- Wins (qualitative):
- Frictions / blockers:
- Next week experiments / calendar changes:

Retrospective notes (2025-02-21):
- Did a 2-day run with RPC buffers and muted slack for afternoon 1. Result: felt calmer; logged two 90-min blocks but interrupted once for Ops page.
- PR throughput: opened one small perf PR (benchmarks attached) — reviewer lag still ~48h. Need to align with reviewers early in the PR description.
- Observations: meetings tend to cascade; losing 25–40m after any scheduled call for context rebuilding.

Action items (short):
- Add default "RPC 25" buffer rule to my calendar for all meeting invites (self-imposed) — DONE (2025-02-19).
- Run a tiny weekly digest: one-line status + three asks for reviewers posted Friday afternoon (template at linked PR).
- Try offline async standup Monday—Asha agreed to pilot on 2025-02-24.
- Add quiet hours: 13:00–15:00 local (notifications off).

Measurement plan details:
- Tooling: RescueTime for passive block detection, manual check-ins in this doc, PR metrics from GitHub Actions, simple spreadsheet (sheet link stubbed in linked_artifacts).
- Tagging: prefix PR titles with [FocusLab] for tracking.
- Noise handling: when an on-call page interrupts, label that day as exception (do not count as failed experiment).

Risks and failure modes: 
- Team dependency: if reviewers don't adopt faster cycles, PR time-to-merge KR will be unreachable without coordination. Mitigation: negotiation and reviewer SLAs for FocusLab PRs.
- Meeting culture: default meetings shift times to avoid my buffers; need to communicate rules and not be passive.
- Measurement noise: RescueTime mislabels meetings; fallback: manual stopwatch logging for critical days.

Notes to self (bullet fragments):
- Keep prompts for PRs short: problem statement, impact, perf delta, test plan, reviewers.
- If energy dips below 4 EOD two days in a row -> scale back calendar armor hours and take one full micro-day off (reset).
- Celebrate small wins: landed a 7% p50 perf win earlier — wire that into sprint demo.

Unresolved questions:
- What's a fair reviewer SLA for FocusLab PRs? 24h weekdays? 48h? (talk with Mikael).
- Can platform team ops create a quiet pager routing for developer deep-focus windows? (raise in SRE sync).

Sample weekly snapshot (2025-02-28):
- Deep-hours: 8.3
- Context switches/day median: 11
- PRs: opened 2 (one merged 30h, one pending 52h)
- Energy avg: 6.8
- Notes: big jump in deep-hours after calendar armor; still seeing reviewer delays.

Longer-term ambition: formalize a small internal playbook for personal attention management we can share with teammates who struggle with context switching. If it moves meta-metrics (throughput, happiness) measurably, propose as a team-wide pilot.

Reference snippets / quick templates (paste into PRs / calendar):
- PR title template: [FocusLab] short-title — Impact: "reduces p50 token latency ~8% on dev harness"
- Async standup template: "Yesterday: X; Today: Y; Blockers/asks (1–3)."
- Quiet calendar reply: "Prefer async; can we record notes instead?"

End of doc — checkpoints: revisit KR numbers on 2025-03-11 and decide whether to scale up or iterate on experiment.
